device.manufacturer: CHEMION (CoolLED OEM hardware; companion app by Neofect)
device.name: CHEMION LED Glasses (CHEMION Original / CHEMION HAT)
device.notes:
Programmable LED matrix glasses (CHEMION Original) and an LED cap (CHEMION HAT), controlled over BLE by the CHEMION app (Android package com.neofect.chemion, analyzed v3.0.5). The hardware is CoolLED OEM; some units advertise with "CoolLED" in the name.
TWO DEVICE TYPES, one frame protocol:
  * CHEMION ORIGINAL (glasses) — Nordic UART Service (NUS)
    6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e, write 6e400002-…, notify
    6e400003-…. Matrix 9 rows x 24 cols at 2 bits per pixel (216 px,
    54-byte frame). App descriptor carries a constant 6, believed to be
    the save-slot count (MEDIUM). Chip: Nordic nRF51 series (per the 2015
    ChemionHacking wiki: Cortex-M0 with legacy nRF DFU).
  * CHEMION HAT — service 4b0d67ea-2faf-4b3c-8c53-f6af0f0171f5, write
    4b0d67eb-…, notify 4b0d67ec-… (roles by NUS convention; MEDIUM).
    Matrix 12 x 32 at 4 bits per pixel (384 px, 1536-byte / 0x600 frame) —
    a color device. App descriptor constant 144 (0x90), believed to be
    its slot count (MEDIUM).

FRAME FORMAT (app -> device; one frame per characteristic write, no app-level MTU chunking — the app's BLE layer relies on long writes):
  [0xFA] [cmd] [lenHi] [lenLo] [payload …] [checksum] [0x55] [0xA9]
  * 0xFA constant header, 0x55 0xA9 constant trailer.
  * cmd = command-TYPE byte (not the message ID): request=0x01,
    reply=0x02, stream=0x03, notify=0x04, error=0x05, identify=0x06.
    App->device writes use 0x01, 0x03 (realtime stream) and 0x04
    (sound-reactive stream). HIGH — this map matches the 2015 wiki.
  * lenHi,lenLo = payload length, big-endian.
  * checksum = XOR of all PAYLOAD bytes only (header, cmd and length are
    NOT covered). HIGH — the checksum the ChemionHacking wiki left
    unsolved; recovered from the app's frame builder (eor loop, seed 0).
  * Every payload embeds a 2-byte big-endian MESSAGE ID, and almost every
    payload also carries a constant byte 0x01 (position varies: trailing
    for power-off, leading elsewhere — see the commands).

MESSAGE ID MAP (msgId -> cmd type, payload; verified against the app's frame builder, HIGH unless noted):
  2  request [00 02 01]              power off
  3  request [01 00 03]              battery level query
  4  request [01 00 10 <idx>]        slot op, glasses only; NOTE the
                                     payload embeds module ID 16, same
                                     wire bytes as msgId 16 (MEDIUM:
                                     legacy alias / delete slot)
  5  request [01 00 05]              heartbeat — the app sends this every
                                     5 s per connected device; send it or
                                     expect the link to drop (MEDIUM:
                                     requirement unverified on air)
  6  stream  [01 00 06 <data…>]      realtime frame streaming, glasses
                                     only (HAT gets an empty payload from
                                     this path — its realtime route is
                                     unresolved, MEDIUM)
  7  request [01 00 07]              slot/status query (semantics MEDIUM)
  9  notify  [01 00 09]              sound-reactive streaming marker
                                     (MEDIUM semantics)
  10 request [01 00 0A <data…>]      frame data block (54 B per glasses
                                     frame)
  11 request glasses: [01 00 0B <idx> <frameSizeHi> <frameSizeLo>]
        HAT: empty payload             frames transfer start
  12 request [01 00 0C]              frames transfer end (glasses only)
  13 request [01 00 0D 01 <data…?>]  play frames on slot (glasses only;
                                     trailing data optional, MEDIUM)
  14 request [01 00 0E <idx>]        slot op with index (play/delete,
                                     glasses only)
  16 request [01 00 10 <idx>]        slot op with index (free space /
                                     delete)
  20 request [01 00 14 <idx>]        slot-frame upload start (both types)
  21 request [01 00 15]              slot-frame upload end (glasses only)
Three further msgIds are loaded from static fields the disassembly does not resolve (likely 1, 8 and 15 or 17 — status, old heartbeat, delete slot / start DFU per the 2015 wiki's enum). The 2015 wiki's message enum (STATUS 0x01 … START_DFU 0x11) broadly matches the low IDs; the current app renumbers/extends (heartbeat is 5; 20/21 are new).
RX (device -> app): notifications arrive on 6e400003-… (glasses) / 4b0d67ec-… (HAT). Parsing was not fully traced; expect the same 0xFA … 0x55 0xA9 framing with cmd=reply(0x02)/notify(0x04)/error(0x05), and a reply to msgId 3 carrying battery level (the 2015 wiki lists BATTERY_LEVEL=0x03). MEDIUM — verify with one live capture.
NO ENCRYPTION on the BLE link. The AES/CRC32 code in the app is a stock ZIP decoder used to unpack downloaded content packs, not the protocol.
OTA: NONE in app v3.0.5 — no Nordic DFU service, no firmware assets, no start-DFU message path found. The 2015 app generation had nRF legacy DFU with four Intel-HEX images (ChemionHacking wiki), so the nRF51 bootloader may still be reachable on old stock, but nothing here depends on it.
CLOUD: api.chemi-on.com / content.chemi-on.com (and dev. variants) are a content store and login/SNS layer — downloadable font/sound packs as ZIP. None of it is needed for control: the BLE protocol above is the whole control surface. No Wi-Fi/UDP/SSDP/mDNS transport exists in the app.
CONFIDENCE SUMMARY: frame format, checksum, cmd-type map and the msgId payload skeletons above are HIGH (read directly from the app's frame builder). Write/notify characteristic roles (NUS convention), slot-count constants, heartbeat requirement, RX layout, 2bpp/4bpp pixel encodings and per-slot-op semantics are MEDIUM pending live capture.

credentials.notes: No authentication of any kind: anything within radio range can connect and issue commands, including power-off. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No reset procedure is documented and none was found in the app — there is no credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central (one BLE link at a time).

steps.action: Power the device off and on again.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: Scan for the advertised name prefixes (CHEMION / HAT / CoolLED) or the service UUIDs, connect, enable notifications on the notify characteristic (6e400003 glasses / 4b0d67ec HAT), and write frames to the write characteristic (6e400002 glasses / 4b0d67eb HAT). The app additionally sends a heartbeat frame every 5 seconds.

steps.action: Power the device on and scan for its advertisement.
Connect, enable notifications on the notify characteristic, then send heartbeat every 5 s.

setup.notes: No provisioning. The device advertises when powered on and the app connects directly, enables notifications on the NUS TX characteristic and starts the 5 s heartbeat. No account, PIN or bonding step was found in the app flow. MEDIUM — inferred from the app's connect path, not yet replayed on hardware.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the device to an owner or network; switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old phone keeps grabbing the link, remove the device from its OS Bluetooth list — a cached bond can hold the single available connection.

testing.notes: Everything here comes from static analysis of the Android companion app v3.0.5 (2026 research store) cross-checked against the public 2015-era reverse engineering at github.com/gsuberland/ChemionHacking. No live capture has been replayed against hardware by this project; the RX (device-to-app) direction in particular is inferred, not traced.

entities.name: LED Matrix
entities.notes: The protocol's only plain power command is OFF (msgId 2); no power-on command exists in the app's message map, so waking the device is the physical button. Everything else is display content: realtime frame streaming (stream_frame), slot upload/play/delete, battery query and heartbeat. No brightness or color commands were found — color lives in the HAT's 4bpp frame data, and glasses intensity in its 2bpp pixels.

entities.name: HAT LED Matrix
entities.notes: Same surface as the glasses entity, on the HAT's own service. Content is 12x32 @ 4bpp color frames.

helpful_urls.description: Open-source prior art: 2015-era app v1.x teardown covering the same frame header/trailer and command-type map, the nRF51 chip identification, and the legacy DFU images. Its one open question — the packet checksum — is answered in this spec: a plain XOR over the payload bytes.

battery_query.description: Query battery level (msgId 3); reply arrives on the notify characteristic (layout MEDIUM, unverified).

frame_data_block.description: One frame of a slot upload (msgId 10). Payload [01 00 0A] + frame bytes (54 per glasses frame); len = 3 + frame byte count. Sent between a transfer-start (msgId 11 or 20) and transfer-end (msgId 12 or 21); the exact start/end pairing per flow is MEDIUM.

frame_data.description: Frame pixels, 2 bits per pixel, 54 bytes for a full glasses frame. Encoding orientation MEDIUM.

len_hi.description: Payload length, high byte = (3 + frame_data length) >> 8.

len_lo.description: Payload length, low byte — 57 for a full 54-byte glasses frame.

glasses_transfer_end.description: Frames transfer end (msgId 12, glasses only). XOR checksum 0x0D.

glasses_transfer_start.description: Frames transfer start (msgId 11, glasses only — the app emits an empty payload for the HAT here). Payload [01 00 0B] + slot index + 2-byte big-endian frame size (54 for glasses).

frame_size_hi.description: Frame payload size, high byte (54 = 0x0036 for glasses).

frame_size_lo.description: Frame payload size, low byte (54 for glasses).

slot_index.description: Target save slot. 6 slots per the app descriptor constant (MEDIUM).

heartbeat.description: Keep-alive (msgId 5). The app sends this every 5 s per connected device; mirror that cadence (requirement MEDIUM).

play_slot.description: Play stored frames (msgId 13, glasses only). Payload [01 00 0D 01]; the app can append optional trailing data whose semantics are unresolved (MEDIUM) — this value sends none.

power_off.description: Power the glasses off (msgId 2). Worked frame: payload [00 02 01], XOR checksum 0x03.

slot_frame_upload_end.description: End of a slot-frame upload (msgId 21, glasses only). XOR checksum 0x14.

slot_frame_upload_start.description: Start of a slot-frame upload (msgId 20; applies to both device types). Payload [01 00 14 <index>].

slot_free_or_delete.description: Slot operation with index (msgId 16) — free-space/delete family. Payload [01 00 10 <index>]. Note: msgId 4 emits these same wire bytes (legacy alias, MEDIUM).

slot_op.description: Slot operation with index (msgId 14, glasses only) — play/delete family. Payload [01 00 0E <index>].

slot_index.description: Slot to operate on (6 slots, MEDIUM).

slot_query.description: Request with payload [01 00 07] (msgId 7). Exact semantics MEDIUM — slot/status query family; no index is appended in app v3.0.5.

stream_frame.description: Realtime stream one frame (msgId 6, cmd type stream 0x03). Payload [01 00 06] + frame bytes. Glasses frame is 54 bytes (9x24 @ 2bpp); len = 3 + frame byte count (0x0039 for a full glasses frame). Glasses only — on the HAT this path emits an empty payload (MEDIUM).

frame_data.description: Frame pixels, 2 bits per pixel, 9x24 = 54 bytes for a full frame. Bit order/orientation MEDIUM — verify against the 2015 wiki and live capture.

len_hi.description: Payload length, high byte = (3 + frame_data length) >> 8.

len_lo.description: Payload length, low byte — 57 for a full 54-byte glasses frame.

stream_sound_marker.description: Sound-reactive streaming marker (msgId 9, cmd type notify 0x04); sent on the sound-reactive path before/alongside realtime frames. Semantics MEDIUM.

characteristics.name: Command Write
characteristics.notes: NUS RX (device side): the app writes complete frames here in a single write each (its BLE layer permits long writes; there is no app-level chunking). Frame: [0xFA][cmd][lenHi][lenLo][payload] [XOR of payload][0x55][0xA9]. NO characteristic-level `framing` is declared on purpose — like the SPOTLED spec, every command below is a COMPLETE frame written verbatim, header and trailer included. cmd byte values: request=0x01, stream=0x03, notify=0x04. Confidence: frame format and these payloads HIGH (from the app's frame builder); per-command semantics as noted.

characteristics.name: Notify
characteristics.notes: NUS TX (device side): the app enables notifications immediately after connecting. Parsing was not fully traced (MEDIUM): expect the same [0xFA][cmd][len][payload][XOR][0x55 0xA9] framing with cmd=reply(0x02)/notify(0x04)/error(0x05); battery level should arrive as a reply to msgId 3 (the 2015 wiki lists BATTERY_LEVEL=0x03). Verify layout with one live capture before decoding fields.

battery_query.description: Query battery level (msgId 3); reply on the notify characteristic (layout MEDIUM).

frame_data_block.description: One frame of a slot upload (msgId 10). Payload [01 00 0A] + frame bytes (1536 per HAT frame); len = 3 + frame byte count.

frame_data.description: Frame pixels, 4 bits per pixel color, 1536 bytes for a full HAT frame. Nibble order / palette MEDIUM.

len_hi.description: Payload length, high byte — 0x06 for a full HAT frame.

len_lo.description: Payload length, low byte — 0x03 for a full HAT frame.

heartbeat.description: Keep-alive (msgId 5); the app sends it every 5 s (requirement MEDIUM).

power_off.description: Power the HAT off (msgId 2). Same frame as the glasses.

slot_frame_upload_start.description: Start of a slot-frame upload (msgId 20; both device types). Payload [01 00 14 <index>]. HAT slot count believed 144 (app descriptor constant 0x90, MEDIUM).

slot_index.description: Slot being uploaded (up to 144 slots, MEDIUM).

slot_free_or_delete.description: Slot operation with index (msgId 16) — free-space/delete family. Payload [01 00 10 <index>].

slot_index.description: Slot to free/delete (up to 144 slots, MEDIUM).

stream_frame.description: Realtime stream one frame (msgId 6, cmd type stream 0x03). HAT frame is 1536 bytes (12x32 @ 4bpp color); len = 3 + frame byte count (0x0603 for a full frame). MEDIUM — the app emits an empty payload on this path for the HAT, so the HAT realtime route may actually be frame_data_block (msgId 10); verify.

frame_data.description: Frame pixels, 4 bits per pixel color, 12x32 = 1536 bytes for a full frame. Nibble order / palette MEDIUM.

len_hi.description: Payload length, high byte — 0x06 for a full 1536-byte HAT frame (0x0603).

len_lo.description: Payload length, low byte — 0x03 for a full HAT frame.

transfer_start.description: Frames transfer start (msgId 11) as the app emits it for the HAT: EMPTY payload (length 0, checksum 0). MEDIUM — the HAT upload path more likely starts with slot_frame_upload_start (msgId 20).

characteristics.name: Command Write
characteristics.notes: Write characteristic for the HAT (role by NUS-style convention; MEDIUM — verify on air). Same frame format as the glasses: [0xFA][cmd][lenHi][lenLo][payload][XOR of payload][0x55][0xA9]. Matrix 12 x 32 @ 4bpp color = 1536-byte (0x600) frames, so a full frame message is ~1546 bytes — it only fits via a negotiated MTU / long write (the app's BLE layer permits long writes; no app-level chunking). Commands below mirror the glasses set with HAT frame sizes; msgId 11 carries an EMPTY payload on the HAT, so its transfer start is slot_frame_upload_start (msgId 20) instead (MEDIUM).

characteristics.name: Notify
characteristics.notes: Notify characteristic for the HAT (role by NUS-style convention; MEDIUM). Same expectations as the glasses notify characteristic: 0xFA-framed replies/notifications/errors. Verify on air.
